titulo: Rewind a Cassette With a Pencil: How Many Turns?
descripcion:
Remember rewinding a cassette with a pencil? Tin and Tan work out how many turns it really takes.
A nostalgia check for anyone who grew up with cassettes in the 1970s, 80s and 90s.

The math, step by step:
- A C90 tape plays 45 minutes per side, which is 2,700 seconds.
- Tape speed: 1 7/8 inches per second (4.76 cm/s), the standard speed of the compact cassette.
- 2,700 s x 1 7/8 in/s = 5,062 inches, about 421 feet of tape.
- One pencil turn winds about 4 1/3 inches (pi x 1.38 in).
- 5,062 in divided by 4 1/3 in is about 1,170 turns.
- At 2 turns per second: about 585 seconds, almost 10 minutes. For one side.

This is an estimate. It assumes an average spool diameter of about 1.38 inches (3.5 cm), which grows as the tape winds. Real tapes and real hands vary.

Source for the tape speed: Philips Technical Review, vol. 31, 1970: "The design of the Compact Cassette is based on a tape speed of 4.76 cm/s."
https://www.musicaememoria.com/docs/PTechReview-31-1970-077.pdf

Voices are AI-generated. The drawings, music and sound effects are original, made with code.

Voces: Higgsfield seed_audio, Kevin (Tin) y Zelda (Tan), 4,8 créditos en total; los términos de uso comercial de Higgsfield se vieron solo en resumen de buscador: leer el texto completo antes de publicar. Fuente de 4,76 cm/s: Philips Technical Review vol. 31, 1970 (vista en resumen de buscador; abrir el PDF antes de publicar). El diámetro promedio de 3,5 cm es un supuesto declarado en la descripción; el resultado es una estimación. Objetivos: metas iniciales sin datos propios (canal nuevo), definidas por el director creativo y comercial; el KPI principal es visto frente a deslizado.
